To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intensity of pain reported by ambulance despatchers to the emergency medical service (EMS) is a predictor of the outcome of patients who call for ambulance because of acute, non-traumatic chest pain.
the presence of pain and associated symptoms in patients who call an ambulance because of chest pain are related to the presence of acute coronary syndrome (ACS).

the presence of pain in the jaw, neck, or upper abdomen, or of dyspnea, was significantly associated with the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction in patients who called for an ambulance because they had acute chest pain.
